result:
It is currently impossible to name the single largest planet in the entire universe because we have only explored a tiny fraction of it. However, astronomers have discovered several "super-Jupiters" and gas giants in our own galaxy that are far larger than Jupiter.

One of the largest known exoplanets is **ROXs 42Bb**, a gas giant estimated to be roughly 2.5 times the radius of Jupiter and about 9 times its mass. Another contender is **GQ Lupi b**, which is even more massive, though there is ongoing scientific debate about whether it is a very large planet or a small "brown dwarf" (a failed star).

In general, there is a physical limit to how large a planet can get. If a gas giant accumulates too much mass, the pressure and temperature at its core become high enough to trigger nuclear fusion, at which point it ceases to be a planet and becomes a star.
